hypothesis: The active v14 all-asset transfer is currently expressing one shared cross-asset fade hypothesis rather than four independent opportunities: BTC, ETH, SOL, and HYPE all entered short from the same provider while the authoritative completed 5-minute breakout side was long and the slower hourly structural direction was short. Resolving these four protected lifecycles can test whether persistent post-entry regime opposition identifies weak fade entries without changing the authorized strategy mid-lifecycle.
decision: Preserve the active v14 runtime and every venue stop while the four open lifecycles resolve. Treat the portfolio as one 100% same-provider, same-side signal cluster in operator telemetry, not as four independent bets. Do not add a regime-opposition exit, profit lock, entry veto, sizing change, or automatic pause from this open prefix: every trade has 21-26 consecutive opposed completed decisions, but none has reached the predeclared 25 bps profit-lock activation and no full-lifecycle outcome exists yet. Keep the exact completed-five-minute momentum exit rejected, keep support-decay and L2 policies report-only, and keep evidence-routed v18 inactive. The next decision must compare the resolved cluster with its entry, opposition, MFE/MAE, friction, and missed-capture paths; this revision does not place, close, resize, gate, restart, or promote anything.
falsifier: The shared-fade mechanism attribution is falsified by any entry whose frozen provider, side, completed 5-minute breakout side, structural direction, or decision timestamp differs from the immutable audit. The concern about persistent opposition is weakened if these unchanged lifecycles recover and close profitably after measured fees, funding, and stop precedence, and strengthened if opposed entries repeatedly lose while comparable aligned entries remain positive. No exit or entry-policy change is supportable unless a predeclared, non-overlapping, profile-matched sample improves after-friction return and drawdown on both long and short paths without single-cluster concentration.
limitations: All four current lifecycles are open, so marked PnL, MFE, MAE, opposition duration, and every exit comparison can change before actual closes.
The four entries are strongly dependent: three share one decision timestamp and all four share one provider, direction, and broad market move.
The v14 run still has only two closed losses and no completed long, so it cannot establish bidirectional edge, repeatability, or portfolio expectancy.
Regime opposition is a descriptive fixed-weight score; association with later outcomes does not prove that an opposition exit improves execution.
The HYPE support-decay retrace comparison pools ten mixed-profile lifecycles and still reduces mean normalized return by at least 32.6 bps versus actual exits.
The aligned-book forward challengers are short-only BBO simulations rather than private IOC fills and remain below profit factor one.
No live strategy, position, order, stop, target, sizing policy, backend process, checkpoint process, or portfolio configuration changed as a result of this revision.
